newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania PM vows action against opposition.
newsitem.headline: Albania PM vows action against opposition.

text.p: Albanian Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi on Wednesday denounced protests against his government and pledged the ruling Democratic Party was waging a fight against moves by the opposition to restore communism.

Meksi told Reuters Television his party was best placed to mobilise the Balkan country despite the refusal of some of its parliamentarians to endorse emergency measures to quell unrest in the southern port of Vlore. Three people have died.
"We have a meeting today of the (leadership) of the Democratic Party to discuss the mobilisation of all the parties against communism," he said.

"Our party has proposed talks with other parties...but they have chosen violence, not dialogue. They want a civil war. We think our party is the strongest in Albania. We think Albanians are for democracy, not for violence."

Demonstrators blaming Meksi's government for the loss of life savings in failed pyramid investment schemes waged street battles for two days this week in Vlore. The collapses have left hundreds of thousands of Albanians destitute.

Parliament, dominated by President Sali Berish's Democratic Party, on Tuesday refused Meksi's proposal to introduce emergency measures in the city after local deputies objected. Albanian leaders say the unrest is the work of leftist extremists.
Several thousand protesters massed in the city on Wednesday in what has become a daily routine but there were no incidents.

The opposition Forum for Democracy alliance, led by the Socialist Party, scheduled a midday rally in a Tirana stadium. But authorities banned the gathering and it was not certain opposition leaders would proceed with it.
Truckloads of riot police moved through the city.
Meksi said the Democratic Party was ready to counter the rally "with our forces, not only the police".

Albanian demonstrators, he said, differed from opposition forces whose protests won concessions from authorities in nearby Serbia and Bulgaria in that they were intent on torpedoing the national economy.
"The Socialist Party wants to organise meetings every day in Tirana because they think Vlore is Belgrade or Sofia," he said.

"But the problem is we are not in the same position. And in Belgrade and Sofia they protest in the evening. They work and protest. (The opposition) wants to block all economic and social life in Albania and to create problems."
Meksi has taken on an increasingly public role over the past few days, while Berisha has appeared to stay out of the spotlight as the crisis in Europe's poorest nation deepened.
